text: Education in Sweden is structured around a nine-year compulsory comprehensive school (grundskola) from ages 6 to 15, offering a balanced curriculum with 16 compulsory subjects including Swedish, mathematics, English, and physical education. Preschool is free for children aged 1–6, with additional hours available for working parents. Upper secondary education (gymnasieskola), lasting three years, offers 18 national programs—mostly preparatory (for university) and vocational—requiring students to pass core subjects and complete a diploma project. Higher education includes university and university college degrees aligned with the Bologna Process, with bachelor’s, master’s, and doctoral levels. Public universities and colleges provide academic degrees, while vocational education offers professional qualifications. Independent schools (friskolor), funded by municipalities, are common and offer diverse pedagogical approaches, though their profitability and grading standards have drawn scrutiny. The system emphasizes equity, inclusion, and quality, with national assessments and anti-discrimination policies in place. Sweden ranks highly in international education assessments, though recent concerns about test integrity and performance fluctuations have prompted ongoing reforms.
